title: Dictator versus no-notables test
statement: Let $\Psi$ be a finite set of sign predicates, let $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<\alpha<\beta\le1$, and let $e\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ map $[0,1]$ into $[0,1]$ and tend to $0$ as its argument tends to $0$ through positive values. Suppose a tester is specified for every positive dimension, uses only predicates in $\Psi$, accepts every coordinate dictator with probability at least $\beta$, and accepts every function with no $(\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$-notable coordinate with probability at most $\alpha+e(\varepsilon)$ for every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$.
hypotheses_covered: The allowed predicate set is finite
The error function tends to zero at zero through positive values
Every positive dimension has a tester
Every check uses a predicate in $\Psi$
Every coordinate dictator is accepted with probability at least $\beta$
For every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$, every function with small stable influences at thresholds $(\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$ is accepted with probability at most $\alpha+e(\varepsilon)$
